---
title: "Mean-based deconvolution comparators"
---

## What is being compared {#sec-deconv-models}

DeCovarT deconvolves bulk profiles with both a mean signature and a
per-type covariance. The comparators in this part do **not**. They
estimate a composition $\boldsymbol{p}$ from a mean signature built on
the same labelled single-cell reference, and they are the baseline
against which a covariance model has to move the estimate.

Three second-generation algorithms are planned on GSE229386, at 48 h,
72 h and 96 h, for the standard Wnt pulse and the early pulse
(@sec-geo-design):

1.  **BayesPrism** — a Bayesian model that treats the single-cell
    reference as a prior on cell-type expression and updates that prior
    with the bulk counts.
2.  **SCDC** — a weighted non-negative least-squares ensemble that can
    combine more than one single-cell reference. Here there is only
    one reference, so the ensemble weight is not a second biological
    replicate.
3.  **DWLS** — dampened weighted least squares, which down-weights
    genes whose mean expression would otherwise dominate the fit.

Literature keys for these three methods are **not yet** in
`bibliography/REFERENCES.bib`. Add them from Zotero before a review
pass; do not cite them by invented keys.

None of the three returns $(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j})$.
They are composition estimators. Sensitivity of those compositions to a
misspecified precision is the last chapter of this part
(@sec-sensitivity). The early-versus-standard reading of their output
is @sec-bio-deconv.

No proportions are reported here. Scripts stay `eval: false` until the
bulk and signature objects exist.
